data.title: Merck CEO Plays Down Cost Concerns Over Intismeran — ‘We Don't See Cost As A Limit To Access’
data.description:
Key points:
  • On Thursday, MRNA shares plunged more than 17% after Phase 3 trial data was leaked ahead of Saturday’s ESMO presentation.
  • Intismeran, combined with Keytruda, reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 58% after six months, compared with Keytruda alone.
  • Merck and Moderna anticipate potential approval of the drug in 2027.

Merck (MRK) CEO Rob Davis expressed confidence in the commercial potential of the much-talked-about personalised cancer vaccine, Intismeran, playing down concerns that its complex manufacturing process could make the treatment too expensive for patients.

His comments came after Citi questioned whether the vaccine’s clinical benefits justify the cost and complexity of production.

In an interview with CNBC on Friday, Davis credited Moderna’s mRNA technology and specialized manufacturing process for making personalized cancer vaccines commercially viable.

“We think we will have very competitive costs, and we don’t see cost as a limit to access,” Davis said.

At the time of writing, MRK shares were down 2.2% while MRNA stock traded 0.1% lower.

Davis ‘Very Confident’ On Delivering Vaccine On Scale

Intismeran is a personalized cancer vaccine being developed using Moderna’s mRNA technology. The two companies are jointly developing the treatment, which is being tested alongside Merck’s blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda. Unlike traditional vaccines, Intismeran is customized using genetic mutations identified in each patient’s tumor.

Davis said the process currently takes about six weeks, from analyzing a patient’s tumor to manufacturing the vaccine. “So it’s actually very efficient, and one, we feel very confident, we can deliver on scale,” Davis added.

Intismeran, Keytruda Reduced Risk Of Melanoma Recurrence Or Death By 58% After Six Months

On Thursday, MRNA shares plunged more than 17% after Phase 3 trial data, which was leaked ahead of Saturday’s ESMO presentation, fell short of investors’ expectations, triggering what analysts described as a “sell-the-news” reaction.

Merck and Moderna subsequently released the official findings, with Intismeran, combined with Keytruda, reducing the risk of cancer returning or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The results were even better after six months, with the combination reducing the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 58%, compared with Keytruda alone.

“What’s not appreciated is because this is an immunisation, much like you would get if you got a vaccine, you really need to look at the six-month data. That’s the time that allows your body to fully mount an immune response at six months, and it has reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 58%. So this is meaningful if you’re a patient,” Davis said.

Potential Approval in 2027

Davis said Merck and Moderna are moving quickly to seek regulatory approval for Intismeran, with hopes of filing an application before the end of 2026.

"We’re working as fast as we can right now to get the file in,” Davis said, adding that the companies anticipate potential approval sometime in 2027.

Retail’s Take On MRNA, MRK

Retail sentiment surrounding MRK on Stocktwits remained ‘bullish’ over the past 24 hours while sentiment for MRNA turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ over the same period.

Chatter largely centered on the data, which left some users disappointed.

View this Stocktwits post
View this Stocktwits post

While MRK shares have climbed 36% so far this year, MRNA continues to be among the top biotech gainers, with a 550% surge.

data.title: SK Hynix and Samsung likely to boost shareholder returns as demand stays strong: BofA
data.description:
SK Hynix and Samsung have seen their fortunes swell thanks to the boom in the memory market, and Bank of America believes the two South Korean giants could further reward shareholders as a result.

“We see potential catalysts in additional shareholder returns from SK Hynix (a special year-end cash dividend following its recent W40tn buyback) and Samsung Electronics (a new buyback post-3Q cash dividend of W30tn),” Bank of America analysts led by Simon Woo wrote in a note to clients. “Both could address these returns at their respective earnings calls on 28-29 Oct. We expect Korean memory chipmakers to step up dividends and buybacks, given exceptionally low P/E ratios (following severe share- price corrections) and strong growth in FCF (despite concerns about a downturn).”

As of the fourth quarter, the annualized free cash flow for SK Hynix and Samsung has exceeded $150B and $226B, respectively. The analysts believe that SK Hynix will keep its shareholder return splits for buybacks and dividends at 60% and 40%, respectively, and 40% and 60% for Samsung.

SK Hynix is set to report its next quarterly results later this month, and the analysts believe the company will offer up “bullish guidance,” due in part to the successful ramp-up of 12-hi HBM4. There could be additional production of 8-hi HBM4 if Nvidia pays a price premium per bit of around 10%.

Separately, Samsung could see gains in the high-bandwidth memory market and the contract pricing in its long-term agreements offers upside, as deliveries extend out to 2029 and 2030.

data.title: Worthington Steel Confirms Its Kloeckner Strategy Following Shareholder Vote
data.description:
Worthington Steel, Inc. () today announced that the proposed domination and profit and loss transfer agreement (“DPLTA”) between Kloeckner & Co SE (“Kloeckner”) and Worthington Steel GmbH, a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Worthington Steel, did not receive the required shareholder approval at Kloeckner’s extraordinary general meeting in Düsseldorf, Germany. As a result, the DPLTA will not become effective. Worthington Steel remains committed to delivering on the long-term strategic and economic rationale of the transaction. For now, the company will operate within the existing ownership and governance structure and will pursue commercial, procurement, operational and strategic opportunities that can be advanced within that framework and in accordance with applicable law.

“The path forward is clear, and we will begin work immediately,” said Geoff Gilmore, Worthington Steel President and CEO. “The vote will affect the timing, mix and manner in which certain goals can be realized, particularly in the near term, but it does not change our conviction regarding the compelling strategic rationale for the acquisition. We continue to see significant long-term synergy and value-creation potential and will pursue relevant opportunities consistent with the existing governance framework.”

Worthington Steel has included Kloeckner’s financial results in its consolidated financial reporting since completing the acquisition of a majority stake in June 2026. The outcome of the vote does not affect this financial consolidation or its financing arrangements.

Worthington Steel completed its voluntary public takeover offer for Kloeckner on June 3, 2026. Following the subsequent public delisting tender offer, Worthington Steel currently holds approximately 62% of Kloeckner’s share capital and voting rights. Following the vote, Worthington Steel’s existing majority stake in Kloeckner and its strategic commitment to the combination remain unaffected.

At the extraordinary general meeting, Kloeckner shareholders approved the proposed election of five Supervisory Board members who had already been serving on the Board following their court appointment in July 2026. Shareholders also approved amendments to Kloeckner’s Articles of Association intended to simplify ongoing corporate governance.

Further information on the public takeover offer and public delisting offer is available at www.strong-for-good.com.

About Worthington Steel

Worthington Steel () is one of North America's leading value-added metals processing and manufacturing companies. The Company partners with customers to deliver specialized, highly technical solutions across carbon flat-rolled steel, aluminum, stainless steel, long products, heavy plate and electrical steel, to solve complex challenges across a broad range of industries.

Worthington Steel employs approximately 12,000 people and operates approximately 150 facilities, primarily in North America, with additional operations in Europe and Asia. The Company combines extensive processing expertise with advanced manufacturing technologies, including galvanizing, pickling, configured blanking, specialty cold reduction, electrical steel laminations, fabrication and precision processing.

Guided by its people-first Philosophy and a commitment to safety, innovation and continuous improvement, Worthington Steel creates long-term value by delivering trusted solutions for customers, opportunities for employees, returns for shareholders and strength for the communities where it operates.

Important Information: The employee and facility counts above reflect the combined totals of Worthington’s wholly owned businesses, consolidated affiliates including Kloeckner, and unconsolidated affiliate consistent with our past practices.

About Kloeckner & Co

Kloeckner & Co is one of the largest producer-independent metals processors and one of the leading steel service center companies. With its distribution and service network of around 110 warehouse and processing locations, primarily in North America and the “DACH” region (Germany, Austria and Switzerland), Kloeckner & Co supplies more than 60,000 customers. Currently, the Group has more than 6,000 employees. Kloeckner & Co had sales of some €6.4 billion in fiscal year 2025. By consistently implementing its corporate strategy, Kloeckner & Co strives to become one of the leading service center and metal processing companies in North America and Europe. The focus is on continued targeted expansion of the service center and higher value-added business, diversification of the product and service portfolio as well as integration of additional CO2-reduced solutions under the Nexigen® umbrella brand.

Safe Harbor Statement

Worthington Steel wishes to take advantage of the safe harbor provisions included in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 (the “Act"). Statements by Worthington Steel which are not historical information constitute "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Act. All forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties which could cause actual results to differ from those projected. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially include, but are not limited to, limitations on Worthington Steel’s ability to direct Kloeckner’s operations under the existing governance framework; delays in or failure to realize anticipated synergies and other acquisition benefits; and risks, uncertainties and impacts described from time to time in Worthington Steel’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: Wells Fargo, Intuit latest companies to object to their shares being tokenized, document shows
data.description:
Key points:
  • In total, 22 companies have objected to OKXICE stock tokenization, document shows
  • OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture
  • SEC exemption bars platforms from listing tokenized shares if issuer objects

By Hannah Lang

Six more companies, including Wells Fargo , Arm Holdings and Intuit , will not allow their shares to be tokenized on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange , according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters.

The new objections, which have not been previously reported, underscore the growing challenges for tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and can be traded on a blockchain similar to cryptocurrencies, despite the US securities regulator recently approving the novel products.

In total, 22 companies have objected, according to the document, which outlines the rules of the OKXICE venture and which companies have objected. It does not say why the companies objected.

Sixteen of the companies, including Microsoft and Alphabet , are listed on Nasdaq . The others are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, which ICE owns.

Spokespeople for Arm and Intuit did not immediately provide comment. A Wells Fargo spokesperson declined to comment.

TOKENIZATION ADVOCATES TOUT 24/7 TRADING

The cryptocurrency industry has said stock tokenization could revolutionize markets by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly. OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture, dubbed OKXICE, but have encountered objections from issuers.

OKX and ICE filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch tokenized stocks under the agency's new innovation exemption. The exemption allows platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks to operate without complying with many requirements that apply ​to traditional stock exchanges.

Under the exemption, platforms must notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stocks, and cannot proceed if the issuer objects.

Speaking to reporters this week, Andrew Cuomo, co-chairman of the OKXICE joint venture, said given how revolutionary tokenization could be, it was natural for companies to take a "wait and see" approach, CoinDesk reported.

While Nasdaq says it welcomes tokenization in principle, it has said such products should be subject to the existing set of rules and investor protections. It has warned that if improperly regulated, tokenization could fragment liquidity and undermine price discovery, among other issues.

"Given the risks we believe issuers must be cautious about their participation," the company warned in a September FAQ.

A Nasdaq spokesperson pointed Reuters to its FAQ.

Although many overseas tokenized stocks are marketed like stocks, they rarely offer the same rights, disclosures and protections as traditional equities.

Under the SEC's exemption, tokenized stocks must confer the same rights and privileges as ​traditional securities, including the ability to receive dividends and exercise voting rights.

data.title: Bombardier to Invest $270 Million in U.S. Expansion as Trump Softens Stance — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Bombardier plans to invest $270 million to expand its American infrastructure footprint and hire 800 U.S. workers, days after President Trump appeared to soften his rhetoric against the Montreal-based business-jet maker.

The expansion includes a significant step-up in operations in Texas, opening a new service center in Indiana, building a learning hub in Kansas, as well as launching additional infrastructure projects in Connecticut.

In a Truth Social post at 11:41 P.M. Thursday, hours before Bombardier's official announcement, Trump praised Bombardier's plans, stating "Bombardier is investing 270 MILLION DOLLARS, creating THOUSANDS of American Jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana."

Bombardier's expansion will directly add 800 U.S. jobs, 300 by way of new projects and 500 through active recruitment, it said on Friday.

The company estimates it has spent $2.8 billion across its U.S. supply chain in 2025 and expects its new hiring initiative to push total direct and indirect American jobs supported by its operations beyond 33,000, with employment presence across more than 20 states.

The capital push comes a few days after Trump made an apparent reference to the Canadian company at a recent rally.

"I'm going to be helping a certain air company get themselves straightened away," he said to the crowd, after he learned it has significant domestic operations.

Bombardier has repeatedly found itself in the crosshairs during the escalating trade tensions between the Trump administration and Canada.

The latest tensions began after an earlier Trump post on Truth Social last month when he said Bombardier was treating the U.S. like a "piggybank," while taking advantage of U.S. buyers, airports, and infrastructure.

"NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren't good enough!" Trump wrote on Labor Day, urging followers to "Buy American. Fly on American airliners."

Bombardier responded by highlighting its deep U.S. footprint, noting that its jets rely heavily on American-made components such as engines, avionics and other critical aircraft systems. The U.S. is also Bombardier's single largest market for business jets, generating a substantial portion of its overall revenues.

As part of its $270 million U.S. initiative--which includes $50 million dedicated to Kansas--Bombardier recently inaugurated a learning center in Wichita, a new North American hub for learning, developing aerospace talent, enhancing capabilities and supporting the long-term growth of its local operations.

In Fort Wayne, Ind., Bombardier will open its roughly 64,500-square-foot service facility in November, which is expected to accommodate up to six business jets for routine maintenance, avionics installations and emergency repair support.

The company also plans to launch additional footprint-expansion projects in Dallas, Texas and Connecticut.

data.title: SEC To Increase Scrutiny of Advisers Recommending SPV Investments — WSJ
data.description:
By Corrie Driebusch

The Securities and Exchange Commission will prioritize reviewing investment advisers that recommend investments in private companies through special purpose vehicles, it said in its 2027 Examination Priorities on Friday.

It follows SEC examiners asking registered investment advisers for proof that their SPVs own or have exposure to the shares in private companies that they claim to, the Journal has reported. Regulators decided to take a closer look following increased investor complaints and a marketing campaign by such funds ahead of SpaceX's initial public offering in June and Anthropic's planned IPO next month.

In August the Journal reported on an SPV fund that advertised pre-IPO exposure to SpaceX but later told investors the shares were sold before trading in the rocket company began, limiting investors' expected gains.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Notice to convene Lamor Corporation Plc's Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders
data.description:
Lamor Corporation Oyj | Company Release | October 23, 2026 at 18:30:00 EEST

The shareholders of Lamor Corporation Plc are invited to the Extraordinary General Meeting to be held on 13 November 2026 commencing at 10:00 a.m. (Eastern European Time) without a meeting venue as a real-time virtual meeting in accordance with Article 9 of the Articles of Association and Chapter 5, Section 16, Subsection 3 of the Finnish Companies Act. Instructions for participation are presented in this notice under section C "Instructions for meeting participants".

Shareholders may also exercise their voting rights by voting in advance. Instructions for advance voting are set out in Section C of this notice to the Extraordinary General Meeting.

A. Matters to be discussed at the General Meeting

The General Meeting will discuss the following matters:

1. Opening the meeting

2. Calling the meeting to order

3. Election of the persons to scrutinize the minutes and to supervise the counting of votes

4. Recording the legality of the meeting

5. Recording the attendance at the meeting and adoption of the list of votes

6. Authorizing the Board of Directors to decide on the issuance of shares

The company announced on 23 October 2026 that it is contemplating carrying out a directed share issue in accordance with the terms of its financing arrangements and to strengthen its liquidity (the "Share Issue"). The Share Issue would increase the company's equity by a total of at least EUR 5 million (gross). The subscription price of the Share Issue will be resolved on by the company's Board of Directors, and the final subscription price is expected to be 10 per cent lower than the volume-weighted average price of the company's shares on the regulated market maintained by Nasdaq Helsinki Ltd during the 30-day period ending on the publication of the company's Q3 2026 business review on or about 6 November 2026 (inclusive of that date). Calculated up to the closing of the trading day preceding the publication date of the release, 22 October 2026, the Share Issue would illustratively result in the issuance of approximately 7.0 million shares. However, as described in more detail below, the Board of Directors proposes to the Extraordinary General Meeting that no more than 10 million shares may be issued under the share issue authorization, to help provide flexibility if there are changes in market conditions.

The Board of Directors proposes that the Extraordinary General Meeting authorize the Board of Directors to decide on the issuance of shares as follows:

The shares issued under the authorization may be new shares or treasury shares. Under the authorization, a maximum of 10,000,000 shares, which corresponds to approximately 36.4 per cent of all of the shares of the company at the time of this proposal, may be issued. The shares may be issued in one or more tranches.

Under the authorization, the Board of Directors may resolve upon issuing new shares to the company itself. However, the company, together with its subsidiaries, may not at any time hold more than 10 per cent of all its shares.

The Board of Directors is authorized to resolve on all terms of the share issue. The Board of Directors is authorized to resolve on a directed share issue in deviation from the shareholders' pre-emptive rights, provided that there is a weighty financial reason for the company to do so.

The proposed authorization does not invalidate any earlier authorizations entitling the Board of Directors to decide on share issuances or issues of special rights entitling to shares.

The authorization is valid until the close of the next Annual General Meeting, however no longer than until 30 June 2027.

7. Closing the meeting

B. Documents of the General Meeting

This notice, which includes all the proposals of the Board of Directors on the agenda of the Extraordinary General Meeting as well as documents referred to in Chapter 5, Section 21 of the Finnish Companies Act are made available to shareholders on Lamor Corporation Plc's website at https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026.

The minutes of the Extraordinary General Meeting will be available on the abovementioned website no later than on 27 November 2026.

C. Instructions for meeting participants

1. Shareholder registered in the shareholders' register

Each shareholder, who is registered on 3 November 2026 (record date of the Extraordinary General Meeting) in the company's shareholders' register held by Euroclear Nordics Ltd, has the right to participate in the Extraordinary General Meeting. A shareholder whose shares are registered in his/her personal Finnish book-entry account (including equity savings account) is registered in the company's shareholders' register. Changes in the shareholding after the record date of the Extraordinary General Meeting do not affect the right to participate in the Extraordinary General Meeting or the shareholder's voting rights.

Registration for the Extraordinary General Meeting commences on 26 October 2026 at 10:00 (Eastern European Time). A shareholder, who is registered in the shareholders' register of the company and who wants to participate in the Extraordinary General Meeting, must register for the Extraordinary General Meeting no later than on 6 November 2026 at 16:00 (Eastern European Time) by which time the registration must be received.

Shareholders may register for the Extraordinary General Meeting by the following means:

a) Via the website https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026.

Online registration requires that the shareholders or their statutory representatives or proxy representatives use strong electronic authentication either by Finnish, Swedish or Danish bank ID or mobile certificate.

b) By e-mail

Shareholders registering by e-mail shall submit the registration form and advance voting form available on the company's website at https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026 or equivalent information to egm@innovatics.fi.

c) By mail

Shareholders registering by mail shall submit the registration form and advance voting form available on the company's website at https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026 or equivalent information to Innovatics Ltd, General Meeting / Lamor Corporation Plc, Ratamestarinkatu 13 A, FI-00520 Helsinki, Finland.

The shareholder and their representative are required to provide information, such as the shareholder's name, date of birth or business ID, phone number and e-mail, address, the name of any assistant or proxy representative and the proxy's date of birth, phone number and e-mail address. The personal data provided by shareholders to Lamor Corporation Plc or Innovatics Ltd is only used in connection with the General Meeting and the processing of the necessary registrations related thereto.

Further information on registration and advance voting is available by telephone during the registration period of the General Meeting by calling Innovatics Ltd at +358 10 2818 909 on weekdays from 9:00 to 12:00 and from 13:00 to 16:00.

2. Holders of nominee-registered shares

A holder of nominee-registered shares is entitled to participate in the General Meeting on the basis of the shares which would entitle them to be entered in the shareholders' register held by Euroclear Nordics Ltd on the record date for the General Meeting 3 November 2026. Participation also requires that the shareholder is temporarily registered in the shareholders' register held by Euroclear Nordics Ltd by 10 November 2026 by 10:00 (Eastern European Time) at the latest. In the case of nominee-registered shares, this is considered as registration for the General Meeting. Changes in the shareholding after the record date of the General Meeting do not affect the right to participate in the General Meeting or the shareholder's voting rights.

A holder of nominee-registered shares is advised to request well in advance the necessary instructions from their custodian bank regarding temporary registration in the register of shareholders, the issuing of proxies and voting instructions, registration at the General Meeting as well as participating in the virtual meeting and advance voting. The account manager of the custodian bank shall register the holder of nominee-registered shares who wishes to participate in the General Meeting temporarily in the register of shareholders of the company by the aforementioned date and time at the latest and, if necessary, arrange for advance voting on behalf of the holder of nominee-registered shares before the end of the registration period for holders of nominee-registered shares. Further information is also available on the company's website at https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026.

A holder of nominee-registered shares who has registered for the General Meeting may also participate in the meeting in real time using telecommunication connection and technical means. In addition to the temporary registration in the company’s shareholders’ register, the real-time participation in the meeting requires the submission of the shareholder’s e-mail address and telephone number and, if necessary, a proxy document and other documents necessary to prove the right of representation, by regular mail to Innovatics Ltd, General Meeting / Lamor Corporation Plc, Ratamestarinkatu 13 A, FI-00520 Helsinki, Finland or by email to egm@innovatics.fi before the end of the registration period for the holders of nominee registered shares, so that the shareholders can be sent a participation link and password to participate in the meeting. If a holder of nominee-registered shares has authorized their custodian to cast advance votes on their behalf, such advance votes will be taken into account as advance votes of the nominee-registered shareholder at the Extraordinary General Meeting, unless the holder of nominee-registered shares votes otherwise at the Extraordinary General Meeting.

3. Proxy representatives and powers of attorney

A shareholder may attend the General Meeting and exercise their rights at the Meeting through a proxy representative. A shareholder's proxy may also elect to vote in advance as described in this notice if they so wish. The proxy representative must authenticate to the electronic registration service and advance voting personally with strong authentication, after which they will be able to register and vote in advance on behalf of the shareholder, who they represent. The shareholder's proxy must present dated proxy documents, or otherwise in a reliable manner prove that they are entitled to represent the shareholder at the General Meeting.

Alternatively, the right of representation can be demonstrated by using the Suomi.fi e-Authorizations service available in the electronic registration service. In such cases, a proxy is nominated in the Suomi.fi authorization service at www.suomi.fi/e-authorizations (using the mandate theme "Representation at the Extraordinary General Meeting"). At the service, the authorized person must identify themselves using strong electronic identification in connection with their registration, after which the electronic authorization will be verified automatically. Strong electronic identification can be performed using online banking codes or mobile ID. More information is available on the website www.suomi.fi/e-authorizations.

Model proxy documents and voting instructions are available on the company's website at https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026. If a shareholder participates in the General Meeting through several proxies representing the shareholder with shares held in different securities accounts, the shares on the basis of which each proxy represents the shareholder shall be identified in connection with the registration.

Any proxy documents are requested to be submitted preferably as an attachment with the electronic registration or alternatively by mail to Innovatics Ltd, General Meeting / Lamor Corporation Plc, Ratamestarinkatu 13 A, FI-00520 Helsinki, Finland or by e-mail to egm@innovatics.fi before the end of the registration period. In addition to submitting the proxy documents, the shareholder or their proxy shall register for the General Meeting in the manner described above in this notice.

4. Participation instructions

A shareholder entitled to attend the General Meeting may participate in the meeting and exercise their rights fully during the meeting by remote access.

Remote access to the General Meeting will be provided through Inderes Oyj's general meeting service on the Videosync platform, which includes video and audio access to the General Meeting. Remote access does not require any paid software or downloads. In addition to an internet connection, participation requires a computer, smartphone or tablet with speakers or headphones for sound and a microphone for speaking or presenting questions. One of the following browsers is recommended for participation: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, or Opera. It is advisable to log in to the meeting system well in advance of the meeting.

The participation link and password for remote participation will be sent by e-mail and SMS to the e-mail address and mobile phone number provided at the time of registration to all those who have registered for the General Meeting no later than the day before the General Meeting. Thus, shareholders who have voted in advance can also participate in the General Meeting remotely via telecommunication if they wish. The votes cast by advance voters will be taken into account in the decision of the General Meeting, regardless of whether they participate in the General Meeting remotely or not. If they participate remotely, they will be able to change their advance votes during the meeting if they so wish, should a vote take place.

For more information on the general meeting service, additional instructions for proxies representing more than one shareholder, contact details of the service provider and instructions in case of possible disruptions can be found here: https://vagm.fi/support. A link to test the compatibility of your computer, smartphone or tablet with the network connection can be found here: https://b2b.inderes.com/knowledge-base/compatibility-testing. It is recommended that you read the detailed participation instructions before the meeting.

5. Advance voting

A shareholder whose shares in the company are registered on his/her personal Finnish book-entry account (including equity savings account) may vote in advance between 26 October 2026 at 10:00 (Eastern European Time) and 6 November 2026 at 16:00 (Eastern European Time) on certain items on the agenda of the Extraordinary General Meeting.

a) via the company's website at https://www.lamor.com/investors/governance/general-meeting/extraordinary-general-meeting-2026. Login to the service is done in the same way as for registration in section C.1 of this notice.

b) or by e-mail by submitting the advance voting form available on the company's website or equivalent information to Innovatics Ltd by e-mail at egm@innovatics.fi.

c) or by mail by submitting the advance voting form available on the company's website or equivalent information to Innovatics Ltd at Innovatics Ltd, General Meeting / Lamor Corporation Plc, Ratamestarinkatu 13 A, FI-00520 Helsinki, Finland.

Advance votes must be received by the time the advance voting ends. The submission of votes by mail or e-mail before the end of the registration and advance voting period shall be considered registration for the General Meeting, provided that it contains the abovementioned information required for registration.

A shareholder who has voted in advance cannot exercise the right to demand a vote under the Finnish Companies Act or ask questions at the General Meeting unless they participate in the General Meeting in person or by proxy at the meeting venue or remotely.

With respect to nominee registered shareholders, the advance voting is carried out by the account manager. The account manager may vote in advance on behalf of the holders of nominee-registered shares whom they represent in accordance with the voting instructions given by them during the registration period set for the nominee-registered shares.

Proposals for resolution that are subject to advance voting are deemed to have been made at the General Meeting without any changes.

6. Other instructions/information

The meeting language is Finnish.

Shareholders present at the General Meeting have the right to ask questions about the matters discussed at the meeting in accordance with Chapter 5, Section 25 of the Finnish Limited Liability Companies Act.

Changes in the shareholding after the record date of the Extraordinary General Meeting do not affect the right to participate in the Extraordinary General Meeting or the shareholder's voting rights.

On the date of this notice to the Extraordinary General Meeting, as of 23 October 2026, Lamor Corporation Plc has a total of 27,502,424 shares and votes. Of these shares, the company holds 542,450 shares, which are not entitled to vote at the Extraordinary General Meeting.

Porvoo, 23 October 2026

Lamor Corporation Plc

Board of Directors

Further information

Fred Larsen, CEO

+358 400 906 311

fred.larsen@lamor.com

Nalle Stenman, CFO

+358 40 566 8918

nalle.stenman@lamor.com

About Us

Lamor is one of the world’s leading providers of environmental solutions. For more than 40 years, the company has helped its customers prepare for environmental damage, respond to it and restore damaged environments on land and at sea.

Lamor provides technologies, services and tailored turnkey solutions for environmental protection, soil remediation and restoration, and material recycling. Its expertise ranges from oil spill response to waste and water treatment, remediation of contaminated soil and chemical recycling of plastics.

Lamor combines the expertise of its own specialists with the execution capability of local partners and its global network. This enables the company to carry out large-scale, rapidly mobilised operations around the world.

Lamor has approximately 550 employees in more than 20 countries. In 2025, the company’s revenue was EUR 90.2 million. Lamor’s share is listed on the main list of Nasdaq Helsinki under the trading code LAMOR.

data.title: Euro zone bonds stabilise as France catches a break
data.description:
Key points:
  • French 10-year yields rise nearly 27 bps this week, biggest euro zone increase
  • German and Dutch 10-year yields fall 7 bps and 6 bps this week
  • Money markets price roughly 80% chance of ECB rate rise by December, LSEG data shows

By Amanda Cooper

Euro zone bonds stabilised on Friday, in a break from the recent volatility caused by concerns over the finances of France and other euro zone countries with large debt burdens.

The risk premium for French and Belgian government bonds this week hit their highest levels in well over a decade.

French yields (FR10YT=RR), which were down 5 basis points at 5.04%, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May.

Meanwhile, Belgian yields (BE10YT=RR) have risen by nearly 19 bps and Italian yields by 11 bps.

At the other end of the euro zone spectrum, German and Dutch 10-year yields (DE10YT=RR), (NL10YT=RR), meanwhile, have fallen 7 bps and 6 bps, respectively.

Friday saw some reversal of the week's trend with German and Dutch yields each up 2 bps at 3.35% and 3.46% respectively.

Next week brings a series of major central bank decisions, including those from the US Federal Reserve, the Bank of Japan and the European Central Bank.

The ECB, along with the other two, is expected to leave rates unchanged, meaning investors will be anxious to hear what President Christine Lagarde says about the outlook, but also about whether stress in French bonds could become a market flashpoint.

"The key argument against another immediate hike is that a significant amount of tightening is already in the system," said analysts at Mizuho.

"Alongside the 50bp of hikes already delivered, long-end yields have risen another 50–75bp, meaning financial conditions are doing some of the ECB’s work. But a pause should not be confused with an all-clear on inflation."

Money markets were back to pricing a roughly 80% chance of a rate rise by December on Friday, LSEG data showed (0#EURIRPR).

This week's 5.6% rise in crude oil futures above $115 a barrel on the back of renewed Houthi attacks on Gulf infrastructure, which would normally weigh on bonds, has been relegated to the background.

Investors are fretting instead over when and how the builders and providers of AI will see a return on the trillions of dollars they are deploying in the rollout, which has reignited government bonds' role as a safe haven, particularly outside the euro zone.

A survey on Friday showed growth across the euro zone's private sector slowed to its weakest pace in four months in October, hurt by an energy-driven rise in costs and a renewed contraction in France, where political and financial instability are picking up.

"Following a spring and summer where the euro zone economy defied expectations, the flash October PMIs pour a little bit of cold water on just how much further sentiment could improve," said Rory Fennessy at Oxford Economics.

"The volatile situation in France weighed heavily on the euro zone picture, with government borrowing costs spiking further as the fiscal situation worsens."

Highlighting the investor preference for non-euro zone assets this week, yields on Japanese government bonds and US Treasuries have fallen more sharply even than German yields, down 13 bps and 10 bps, respectively, while those of Australian bonds are down 4 bps this week.

data.title: Hitachi, Brookfield, Hartree, and Tokyo Gas Launch Collaboration to develop green data centers with on-site power generation to meet rapidly growing AI demand
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Hitachi, Ltd. ("Hitachi"), Brookfield Japan Kabushiki Kaisha("Brookfield"), Hartree Partners Singapore Pte. Limited ("Hartree"), and Tokyo Gas Co., Ltd.("Tokyo Gas") signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 30 regarding collaboration to develop green data centers in Japan ("Collaboration").

The MoU now includes Tokyo Gas, and builds on a previous MoU signed by Hitachi, Brookfield and Hartree(*1), which was announced in July 2025. The MoU demonstrates the continued commitment of all parties to develop green data centers in Japan. Through the MoU, the four companies will formulate a basic concept for power-integrated green data centers that generate their own energy, utilize it reliably and efficiently, and contribute to decarbonization through green energy and other related measures(*1), while promoting the development of a standardized model that can be deployed flexibly. This approach aims to reduce excessive reliance on the power grid, expand data center siting options, promote local production and consumption of energy, shorten project lead times, and enable scalable deployment. As the first projects under the Collaboration, the four companies plan to develop green data center projects in the Kanto and Kyushu regions.

Through the Collaboration, the four companies will combine their respective expertise to address the critical societal challenges of securing power, ensuring stable operations, and promoting decarbonization for AI data centers.

(*1) Press release issued on July 17, 2025: Hitachi, global investment firm Brookfield, and global commodities trading firm Hartree Begin to Explore a Funding Scheme in the Environmentally-friendly Digital Infrastructure Sector

(*2) Specifically, this refers to the implementation of measures contributes to the decarbonization of data centers by offsetting-fully or partially-greenhouse gas emissions generated during the lifecycle of the fuel, from mining to combustion, through the use of carbon credits (carbon offsetting) as well as through the use of non-fossil fuel certificates and other environmental attributes.

Background

In recent years, the spread of AI technologies and accelerating digitalization have driven a surge in data center construction, particularly in urban areas, leading to growing electricity demand in Japan. As longer lead times for securing power capacity due to grid constraints become increasingly apparent, greater importance is being placed on optimizing energy supply-including advanced coordination between power and communications networks at data centers-and enhancing resilience. At the same time, demand for decarbonized data centers is growing. As part of its Green Transformation (GX) initiatives, the Japanese government has advocated for the development of sustainable infrastructure, including the use of green energy and other related measures and the regional decentralization of data centers(*3). In addition to ensuring the reliability of facilities and power supply, the development of flexible infrastructure capable of responding to the accelerating advancement of AI technologies has become an important issue for stable data center operations. To address these challenges, demand is growing for a new model of data center infrastructure that can simultaneously ensure a stable power supply, achieve decarbonization, and meet the demands of AI.

(*3) Source: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, "Future Initiatives for Watt-Bit Collaboration." (https://www.soumu.go.jp/main_content/001050386.pdf)

Further details about the MoU and the strengths of each company

The four companies aim to develop the following standardized model for green data center designed to achieve high reliability across both its energy supply and operations.

(1) Energy supply combining multiple power sources

The four companies will explore a highly reliable and efficient energy supply model that uses on-site generation facilities as the primary power source and combines multiple other sources, including battery storage and grid power.

(2) Redundancy across the entire infrastructure

The four companies will build redundancy into the entire data center infrastructure, including cooling and power distribution equipment, to maintain stable operations in the event of equipment failures or fluctuations in power supply.

(3) Definition of decarbonization requirements

The four companies will define requirements for data center decarbonization, including the utilization of carbon credits, environmental attributes, renewable energy, and other decarbonization measures.

(4) Standardization and modularization of major facilities

By standardizing and modularizing major facilities-including data center buildings and equipment, as well as on-site power plants and related equipment-the four companies aim to shorten data center project lead times and enable scalable deployment according to demand.

For more information: https://www.hitachi.com/content/dam/hitachi/global/en/press/files/2026/10/261019.pdf

Source: Hitachi, Ltd.

data.title: Kilitch Drugs to sell Ethiopia unit for $14 million, eyes GLP-1 and India expansion
data.description:
Kilitch Drugs (India) Limited plans to divest its entire stake in its Ethiopian subsidiary, Kilitch Estro Biotech PLC (KEB), to state-owned HarmeeCare Pharmaceuticals in a transaction valued at $14 million, as it looks to redirect capital towards domestic expansion, debt reduction and entry into high-growth segments such as GLP-1 therapies.

The proposed transaction, approved by the company's board, marks a strategic shift in Kilitch's growth plans. The Mumbai-based drugmaker said the proceeds from the sale would be used to reduce borrowings, lower finance costs and support the phased expansion of its upcoming manufacturing facility at Pen in Maharashtra.

The Pen facility is expected to be central to Kilitch's next phase of growth. The company plans to manufacture liquid injectable vials, lyophilised injectables and ophthalmic products at the site. It also plans to develop and manufacture GLP-1 therapies, a fast-growing category of obesity and diabetes drugs that is attracting significant industry attention as patents on key products begin to expire globally.

The company also intends to pursue EU GMP and PIC/S accreditations to strengthen its presence in regulated export markets, subject to regulatory approvals.

“Our focus is on building the next phase of Kilitch Drugs' growth by strengthening our manufacturing capabilities and expanding our presence in high-potential pharmaceutical segments,” said Bhavin Mehta, whole-time director of Kilitch Drugs (India) Limited.

The divestment will help the company unlock capital, strengthen its balance sheet and accelerate expansion plans in India while creating opportunities in emerging therapy areas and regulated markets, he added.

Despite exiting ownership of the Ethiopian unit, Kilitch does not intend to leave the market entirely. The company said it proposes to enter into a long-term supply and technical services agreement with HarmeeCare Pharmaceuticals, allowing it to maintain a commercial presence in Ethiopia and continue supporting operations at the local manufacturing facility.

The transaction is expected to be completed by January 31, 2027, subject to shareholder approval, regulatory clearances and the execution of definitive agreements.
